lab_title: Exploring Apparent Retrograde Motion of Mars
top_level_objectives: Understand the concept of apparent retrograde motion of planets.
Analyze the historical transition from the geocentric to the heliocentric model of the solar system.
Compare the retrograde motion of Mars to that of Jupiter and Saturn.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of retrograde motion using Mars as the focus.
key_visuals: Artistic representation of ancient geocentric model
student_actions: Listen to a brief overview of retrograde motion and its significance.
Interact with a 3D model of Mars and its apparent motion against the stars.

scenes.brief_purpose: Simulate observing Mars’s retrograde motion from Earth's perspective.
key_visuals: Mars moving eastward then looping westward through constellations
student_actions: Observe the nightly movement of Mars over several weeks.
Tap through different nights to see Mars's changing position.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain how the retrograde motion is an optical illusion caused by the positions of Earth and Mars in their orbits.
key_visuals: Path of Earth around the Sun
Path of Mars around the Sun
Visualizations of the orbits and speeds of Earth and Mars
student_actions: View an animated representation of Earth and Mars orbiting the Sun.
Identify the points of overtaking and observe the resulting apparent motion of Mars.

scenes.brief_purpose: Shift to the heliocentric model to explain retrograde motion’s natural occurrence.
key_visuals: Outward perspective of the solar system
Animations of Earth and Mars moving in orbit around the Sun
student_actions: Rotate the solar system model to observe different perspectives.
Engage with a quiz on how heliocentric motion explains retrograde motion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the retrograde motions of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.
key_visuals: Paths of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn in night sky
Scale graphics showing distance from the Sun
student_actions: Select different planets to view their retrograde paths over time.
Analyze the differences in apparent retrograde motion between the planets.

scenes.brief_purpose: Discuss the impact of retrograde motion observations on astronomical theories.
student_actions: Engage in discussion about the significance of these observations.
Submit reflections on how retrograde motion influenced our understanding of the solar system.
